Caleb Femi is the Young People's Laureate for London. He is also an English teacher, filmmaker and photographer. As a poet, Caleb's commissions include the Tate Mordern, The Royal Society for Literature, St Paul's Cathedral and the Guardian. Caleb has graced major stages such as the Roundhouse mainstage, Barbican, British Library, Royal Festival Hall. He has also opened up for Lianne La Havas and has performed at many festivals including Latitude, Ed Fringe, Boomtown, Lovebox and Greenbelt to name a few. Caleb has also won the Roundhouse Poetry Slam and Genesis Poetry Slam and is currently working on a debut pamphlet. Also, Caleb leads poetry workshops and talks around the UK. As a filmmaker, Caleb has released two documentaries ‘What Did Love Taste Like In The 70s?’ and 'Heartbreak & Grime', to good international reception, which has led him to give talks and panel discussions on the topic of Grime music, Roadman culture and masculinity.

PopChange (Pop Culture & Social Change) is a pioneering initiative led by Counterpoints Arts exploring how the power of pop culture can be harnessed for social change in order to shift the way we talk, think and feel about migration and displacement in the UK. Together with a network of cultural innovators, creators, producers, funders and activists, it champions new ideas and cross-sector collaborations. PopChange is focusing on key areas of UK culture: football, fashion, gaming and comedy, with media and entertainment as a cross-cutting theme.

Across 26 glorious years and two Black Country venues, it has welcomed some of the biggest names in rock; from Joe Bonamassa to Led Zeppelin frontman Robert Plant via Slade, Steven Seagal, Lenny Henry and more. Website accompanies the book' 'Keeping' Music Live'.

Founded by Newcastle Upon Tyne based journalist Johnathan Ramsay in 2016, RIDE Music is the hub for all things underground music and culture related in the UK, US and around the world. Originally created to cover local underground hip-hop in the North East of England, RIDE has evolved over the years to become an international hub for all things alternative hip-hop and underground music. It allows users to find new artists that break boundaries, reject the norm and push underground culture forward you’ve came to the right place. UNDERGROUND UPRISING.

Website includes archive and reading lists created for previous events.

The Floor Magazine is an online and print publication celebrating emerging talents of colour in the literary and creative worlds. Its content doesn't just appeal to its readers, "it highlights the writer, the subject and everyone in between. With a focus on Music, Literature and the Visual Arts (TV and Film) we take pride in meaningful commentary and shaping the narrative on pop culture. We believe what is covered and who covers it ultimately decides what is deemed important news, and creatives of colour have routinely been excluded from the scene. For example, 86% of all Black music creators agree that there are barriers to progression*, and this is just within the UK. ​Through our biannual issues, online coverage, events and video content we are actively taking part in closing the gap for marginalised creatives across all of our focused topics - whilst also cementing ourselves as a cornerstone in future conversations."
